speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been there and if it is changing in size or appearance? Also, have you noticed any fever, chills, or red streaks spreading from the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and recent corticosteroid use for uveitis, this painful ulcerative lesion that appeared after minor trauma (the "ant bite") is highly characteristic of Pyoderma Gangrenosum, a neutrophilic dermatosis often associated with underlying systemic inflammation. I recommend we proceed with a skin biopsy to confirm the diagnosis and rule out infection before initiating treatment.
